props.gloss_en: the dispute [of R' Yehuda and the Rabbis] is where the blessings are identical; where they are not identical, all agree he blesses this one and then blesses that one
R' Yehuda holds a kind of the seven species takes precedence
the Rabbis hold the favoured kind takes precedence
the baraita: if a radish and an olive were before him, he blesses the radish and exempts the olive
the stam: the baraita speaks of where the radish is primary
the baraita's seifa, R' Yehuda: he blesses the olive, for the olive is of the seven species
the mishnah: anything primary with a secondary food alongside -- he blesses the primary and exempts the secondary
the baraita, R' Yehuda: if the olive comes because of the radish, he blesses the radish and exempts the olive

the stam: the radish is indeed primary; the dispute is in another case, and the baraita is lacunose: where the radish is not primary all agree he blesses each; two kinds whose blessings are identical -- whichever he wants; R' Yehuda: the olive, of the seven species
the other: even where the blessings are not identical there is a dispute
R' Yirmeya: [where the blessings differ] they dispute which one precedes
whatever precedes in this verse precedes for blessing, as it says 'a land of wheat and barley, vine, fig and pomegranate, a land of olive oil and honey' (Deut 8:8)
R' Chanan: the entire verse was stated for measures
wheat: the leprous-house mishnah -- the clothes he wears stay pure until he stays as long as eating a pras of wheat bread (not barley), reclining and eating with relish
barley: the mishnah -- a bone the size of a barleycorn defiles by contact and carrying, not by tent
vine: a revi'it of wine for the nazir
fig: a dried fig's bulk for carrying out on Shabbat
pomegranate: the mishnah -- all householders' vessels, their measure is [holes the size of] pomegranates
R' Yosei b. R' Chanina: 'a land of olive oil' -- a land all of whose measures are olive-sized
the stam: rather, a land MOST of whose measures are olive-sized
honey: [the measure] of a large date on Yom Kippur
the stam: are these measures written explicitly? rather, they are rabbinic, and the verse is a mere support (asmachta)
dates and pomegranates were brought before them; Rav Hamnuna took and blessed the dates first
Rav Hamnuna: this [the date] is second to 'land', and that [the pomegranate] fifth to 'land'
Rav Chisda: who will give us iron legs, that we may [serve and] hear you
